acceptance: The first fault is named with cited evidence (CedarDB container logs/exit state or BenchBox-side cause), including whether the image or BenchBox changed between 50fedc71 and 3d7619ee.
If evidence is missing, the UAT captures CedarDB server logs and container state before teardown (as #4285 does for StarRocks) and the cause is named on the next recurrence.
Fix merged (or owner decision recorded), and the cedardb shard passes in two consecutive nightly trunk UAT runs with no rerun (run ids recorded).
context:
2026-11-19: #4392 (merge 82e8b2c5) generalised the pre-teardown capture into tests/uat/engine_evidence.py and added a CedarDB collector (container log across restarts, docker die/oom/restart events, OOMKilled/exit code/restart count/health history, cgroup memory, host). Analysis of 44500662749 vs 44278856759: the server restarted mid-cell three times (tpcds_obt 0.1, coffeeshop 1.0, flightdata 1.0), with restart: unless-stopped bringing it back; no BenchBox, compose or image change between 50fedc71 and 3d7619ee; every cell ran slower in the failing run (tpch 1.0 49->70 s, h2odb 1.0 232->455 s), pointing at a slower or contended runner. OOM under the 8 GiB container limit is the leading hypothesis but unconfirmed: no container log or exit state was retained. Separate defect found: the UAT readiness/liveness probes use psql, which the image lacks (exit 127, always skipped); follow-up fix in progress. Remaining: name the first fault from the next cedardb-evidence bundle on recurrence; two consecutive green nightlies.

2026-11-19: #4394 (merge d4ac7aac) made the CedarDB readiness/liveness probe real (pg_isready, as the compose healthcheck uses) and removed CedarDB's exit-126/127 'tool missing' skip. A dead server between cells now records a failed application-liveness event and the remaining cells as died-mid-platform (existing liveness semantics; stricter than before, where cells after a restart were attempted and could pass). Timeouts, intervals and retries unchanged.

2026-11-22 closing evidence, read live from GitHub: the shard passed on attempt 1, with no rerun, in three consecutive scheduled trunk UAT runs: 44712884700 (2026-11-20, 03b2c0186e), 44888589677 (2026-11-21, 3e09d4f43b) and 45007293835 (2026-11-22, 93f336032a). Owner decision 2026-11-22 (choice dialog): finish this item with the three run ids recorded. The first fault was never confirmed from server-side evidence (out-of-memory under the 8 GiB container limit stays the leading hypothesis); the collector from #4392 captures container logs and exit state for the next recurrence.
description:
Nightly trunk UAT 44500662749 (develop 3d7619ee, 2026-11-19) stage 2 cedardb: 11 of 35 cells failed. tpcds_obt 0.1 and coffeeshop 1.0 failed with 'current transaction is aborted', then 'SSL error: unexpected eof', then 'the connection is closed'. ssb 0.01/0.1, tsbs_devops 0.01/0.1 and datavault 0.01/0.1/1.0 failed to connect: 'server closed the connection unexpectedly. This probably means the server terminated abnormally'. flightdata 1.0 failed after 910 s. Cells between failures passed (ssb 1.0, tsbs_devops 1.0), so the server is crashing and restarting, or dropping connections, intermittently. The previous nightly 44278856759 (50fedc71) passed the cedardb shard. Artifacts: release-uat-trunk-d3817ea0...-stage2-cedardb.

Decision gate: any change to memory limits, timeouts, retries, prunes or container settings needs explicit owner approval before landing. A fix to BenchBox code (connection handling, load path) or a pinned CedarDB image regression with evidence does not.

Guardrails: no cell pruning, retry or timeout increase to turn the shard green; find the first fault from server-side evidence (container logs, exit codes, OOM events, dmesg) before changing anything; compare the CedarDB image digest and BenchBox commits between 50fedc71 and 3d7619ee.
